A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedLUAR research by the same authors. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated classification experiments on four datasets, including accuracy, communication costs, learning curves, and recycling-depth sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, controlled ablations, memory measurements, and heterogeneity and client-count experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes the initial recycling set R0 from all layers to an empty set, allowing fresh updates to be aggregated before recycling begins. The layer-priority metric, stochastic selection rule, and subsequent recycling procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same classification tasks on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, FEMNIST, and AG News. The added heterogeneity and client-count sweeps vary partitions and population sizes within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds FedBAT to the four main benchmark comparisons and PruneFL to the LUAR compatibility comparisons. Tables 4–5 introduce random, positional, gradient-norm, deterministic-selection, and update-dropping comparators. The compatibility table omits its former FedAvg rows. FDA in Table 2 corresponds to the existing FedDropoutAvg baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds fixed-recycling-depth controls, per-process memory measurement, Dirichlet concentration sweeps over 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0, and total-client counts of 64, 128, and 256 with 32 active clients. Existing training settings are retained; AG News using concentration 0.5 was already documented in v1's appendix. These are additional protocols rather than evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained recycling-depth sensitivity analysis, v2 directly tests alternative layer-selection policies, stochastic versus deterministic selection, and recycling versus dropping. Section 3.4 and Appendix A.4 add memory analysis and robustness studies across data heterogeneity and client counts, substantially expanding examination of the method's design choices and operating conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the at-least-three-run statement and tables containing ± values. v2 adds several tables without uncertainty and a checklist statement that only means are reported after three runs, conflicting with its retained ± entries. This changes uncertainty documentation without establishing additional runs, new seeds, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The original main benchmark scores and recycling-depth sweeps retain their values. v2 adds substantial results for FedBAT, PruneFL with LUAR, selection controls, dropping, memory, and robustness. For example, Table 5 reports FEMNIST accuracy of 73.17% with recycling versus 64.69% with dropping at the same normalized communication cost of 0.18 and recycling depth of two layers.

T1.justification: The main-text masked-gradient definition is corrected to refer to recycled layers, matching v1's appendix, rather than zeroing those layers. Section 3.4 also adds the memory-footprint derivation a(d-k)+k versus ad. The existing convergence assumptions, bounds, and appendix proofs retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the convergence claim from a neighborhood of a minimum to a neighborhood of a stationary point. The central recycling contribution, accuracy-preservation claim, and headline AG News communication cost of 17% remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's increased-server-memory limitation with an argument and measurements for lower memory under its aggregation implementation. It changes heterogeneity advice from larger batches to smaller learning rates, explains deterministic recycling failures through excessive staleness, and adds interpretations concerning robustness, scalability, and environmental benefits.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository link and states that code is public. It adds FedBAT hyperparameters, including coefficient 6 and warm-up ratio 0.5, and describes the memory-measurement implementation using 16 local models per process and MPI_Allreduce. Existing software, hardware, optimizer, and training hyperparameter disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion and citations for FedBAT, SpaFL, GossipFL, BCRS, decentralized averaging, and YOGA, explicitly distinguishing YOGA's decentralized setting. It also replaces the cited You et al. CNN training work with the BERT optimization work. The overall positioning around compression and update recycling remains intact.

P1.justification: Much of the introduction, method exposition, conclusion, and proof narrative is retained. v2 polishes language, condenses baseline descriptions, moves the recycling-depth discussion into Appendix A.4, and reframes Section 4.4 as an ablation study. It also adds an appendix roadmap, acknowledgments, broader impacts, and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the paper into the conference layout, wraps text around Figures 1–2, and recolors existing charts. It merges the two compatibility tables, combines the existing AG News and CIFAR-10 curves into Figure 4, and adds memory, ablation, and robustness tables. The former main-text recycling-depth table is removed while its results remain in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v1 asserted advantages for its selection metric and recycling over dropping without direct controlled comparisons. v2 Tables 4–5 supply those tests, substantially strengthening support for the central design choices. Corrected initialization and a narrower convergence claim also improve precision. Inconsistent recycling-depth labels in Tables 13 and 15 and contradictory uncertainty documentation limit reproducibility, but the stronger evidence for the core method supports a substantial net improvement.
